title: Dereferencing and Null Pointers
learningObjectives: Access or modify an object through a valid pointer.
Understand null dereference as undefined behavior.
Use pointer guards and safe defaults.

understand.concept: Dereferencing a valid pointer accesses the object it points to. A null pointer represents no valid object; dereferencing null is undefined behavior.
understand.whyItMatters: Null checks and indirect access help avoid crashes and undefined behavior.
understand.explain: Use nullptr for an empty pointer and check before dereference when null is possible.

practise.guidedTask: For Dereferencing and Null Pointers, draw the object and pointer/reference relationships for every example. Mark owner, target, constness, lifetime, validity of access, and any operation that could invalidate the pointer or reference.
practise.independentTask: Write a focused C++ exercise for Dereferencing and Null Pointers. Demonstrate at least three cases, including a safe usage and a boundary/invalid case explained in comments but not executed. State who owns the resource and when each object/view is valid.
hints: Draw the pointer/reference and its target object.
Mark whether the object is alive and who owns it.
Check nullptr and bounds before access.
Consider invalidation, deletion and scope exit.
Use standard containers or smart pointers when they express ownership more safely.
